title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD Summary, Roadmap & Pricing — Q4 2026 Release Notes
author: Priya Kapoor
content:
Purpose
-------
This document captures the consolidated product overview, PRD summary, design specs, roadmap themes, pricing & packaging notes, and release notes for the Unified Inference product family (hosted API, Dedicated, and Private) for the Q4 2026 release window. Intended readers: product management, engineering, go-to-market, customer success, and partner teams.

Executive summary
-----------------
- Goal: deliver the Unified Inference v1.3 release that improves tail latency for streaming responses, introduces per-route cost controls in the Console, and launches new pricing SKUs for Dedicated reserved capacity.
- Business impact: reduce median tail latency by 15–25% for common chat workloads and enable customers to reduce unit inference costs by up to 20% through batching and cache suggestions in Redwood Optimize.
- Release target: phased rollout starting 2026-12-05 with full availability 2027-01-10.

Product overview (what's included in v1.3)
----------------------------------------
1) Serving improvements
   - Continuous-batching tuning: adaptive batch size that reduces per-token overhead for high-concurrency tenants.
   - KV-prefix caching enhancements: support for partial KV warming for long-context models (up to 64k tokens).
   - Streaming latency optimizations: lower first-byte latency for streaming by ~20ms on average using kernel prefetch paths.

2) Console / Operations
   - Per-route cost controls: enable per-API-route budget limits, cost alerts, and configurable fallback policies.
   - Token-level cost breakdowns in Query Inspector: top token contributors, model selection impact, and quantization guidance.

3) Dedicated & Private
   - New Dedicated SKUs: reserved-small, reserved-medium, reserved-large with Clear SLA tiers (SLA: 99.95% monthly uptime for reserved-medium+).
   - Private deployment tooling: automated config validator for customer manifests and a preflight network check tool (CLI: redwood private preflight --manifest).

PRD summary (requirements & success criteria)
--------------------------------------------
Scope (must-haves)
1. Reduce 95th percentile streaming reply latency by >= 15% for chat workloads (10k qps test harness).
2. Ship per-route cost controls visible in Console and programmable via API (routes.create/update endpoints).
3. Provide Dedicated SKU pricing table and billing events for reserved contracts.
4. Unit integration tests and e2e perf tests in benchmarking suite with clear pass/fail thresholds.

Acceptance criteria (quantitative)
- 95th percentile streaming latency: baseline 350ms -> target <= 300ms for target workloads.
- Billing accuracy: <0.5% variance between reported tokens and billing events in test accounts over 7-day period.
- Scale: reserved-medium SKU supports sustained 2k tokens/sec per instance with <2% error rate.

Design specifications (high level)
--------------------------------
Architecture changes
- Adaptive batching controller: new controller service (batch-controller) that monitors per-worker queue lengths and issues batch window hints via RPC to runtime. Implementation notes: controller is stateless, reads metrics from exporter, uses EWMA for latency prediction.

- KV warm-path: metadata service will store KV-anchor signatures to allow partial prefetch. Runtime will request anchors during prefill; anchors compressed using LZ4.

APIs and schema changes
- routes API additions:
  - POST /v1/routes/{route_id}/cost-control
    payload fields: {"budget_usd_per_day": "<number>", "fallback_policy": "permissive|restrictive|route-fallback", "alert_threshold_pct": "<number>"}
  - GET /v1/inspector/{query_id}/token-breakdown (returns a breakdown object in Console; backend adds a new column to query_events table: token_cost_components)

Security & compliance considerations
- All new telemetry fields must be scrubbed of PII before storage (see security-and-compliance/audit-logging guidance). Offline tests will be run on synthetic datasets.

Operational runbook summary
--------------------------
- Owners:
  - Feature lead: Priya Kapoor (product)
  - Runtime owner: Daniel Li (eng-serving-runtime)
  - Dedicated billing owner: Maya Rodriguez (finance-product)

- SLOs to monitor during rollout:
  - Streaming first-byte latency P95 <= 300ms (global).
  - Error rate across routes <= 1% (5m rolling window).
  - Billing reconciliation latency <= 24 hours.

- Rollout plan (phased):
  1. Canary: 2026-12-05 — internal customer accounts + 5 pilot customers (feature flag: unified_inference_v1_3).
  2. Gradual ramp: 2026-12-12 — expand to 25% traffic for hosted API and selected Dedicated clusters.
  3. Full avail: 2027-01-10 — GA for all self-serve accounts and Dedicated customers after billing contract updates.

Roadmap & themes (next 6–12 months)
----------------------------------
Themes:
- Performance & cost efficiency (Q4 2026 — Q1 2027): batching, cache, quantization profiles driven by workload patterns.
- Enterprise readiness (Q1 2027): expanded Private deployment automation and SOC2 artifacts for Dedicated SKUs.
- Observability & guardrails (Q2 2027): deeper traceability for route-level regressions and automatic rollback triggers.

Milestones:
- 2026-12-05: v1.3 canary rollout (streaming, per-route cost controls).
- 2026-12-20: Dedicated SKU pricing published; sales enablement kit published.
- 2027-01-10: v1.3 GA and billing events live for reserved contracts.
- 2027-03-01: Redwood Optimize integration: automated quantization suggestions for top-10 customer workloads.

Pricing & packaging notes
------------------------
Guiding principles:
- Simplicity for self-serve customers, flexibility for enterprise.
- Pricing tied to unit economics (tokens, compute-backed SKUs) and explicit discounts for reserved commitment.

New SKUs (summary table)
| SKU               | Billing unit                        | Target customer    | SLA            | Monthly list price (USD) |
|-------------------|-------------------------------------|--------------------|----------------|-------------------------:|
| reserved-small    | commitment per-node / monthly       | SMB teams          | best-effort    | 2,500                  |
| reserved-medium   | commitment per-node / monthly       | Growth & midmarket | 99.95%         | 12,500                 |
| reserved-large    | commitment per-node / monthly       | Enterprise         | 99.98%         | 45,000                 |
| hosted-payg       | per-token (prompt+completion)       | Self-serve         | none           | 0.0008 / token         |

Notes and details:
- Reserved SKUs include a baseline of model variants (quantized and FP16) and a burst credit pool for short spikes. Bursts billed at on-demand multiplier (1.5x).
- Enterprise partners may opt for usage discounts up to 40% depending on commit size and term length.
- Cost controls in Console can prevent unexpected overages by enforcing per-route budget caps and auto-fallback to cheaper model variants.

Billing & metering changes
- New billing events record reserve_premium, route_budget_violation, and fallback_trigger. Events schema is versioned (billing_v3).
- Metering accuracy target: reconcile to invoice within 0.5% for pilot accounts (7-day comparison window).

Release notes (what changed, known issues, migration notes)
---------------------------------------------------------
Highlights
- New: per-route cost controls in Console and API.
- Improved: streaming latency reductions via adaptive batching and kernel prefetch.
- New: Dedicated SKUs and billing events for reserved capacity.

Behavioral changes / migration guidance
- Customers using custom routing policies should validate fallbacks after enabling per-route cost controls. Default fallback is model variant 'gpt-mini' if configured as permissive.
- If you rely on exact token counts in older billing pipelines, switch to billing_v3 events and validate on a staging account.

Known issues (tracked in eng-serving-runtime/known-issues)
- Partial KV warm-path may increase memory pressure in some older host types (nv-2080-class); mitigation: limit prefetch to 25% of working set.
- Rarely, adaptive batching may introduce slightly higher median latency for single-request flows when enabled globally; rollout starts behind a feature flag.

Telemetry & alerting additions
- New metrics: route.budget_used_usd, route.fallback_count, streaming.first_byte_latency_ms_p95.
- New alerts (SRE):
  - ALERT: RouteBudgetExceeded — triggers when route.budget_used_usd > budget_usd_per_day * 1.05 for 5m. Owner: eng-platform.
  - ALERT: StreamingP95Degradation — triggers when streaming.first_byte_latency_ms_p95 > 300ms for 15m. Owner: eng-serving-runtime.

Documentation & enablement
-------------------------
- Console docs: add "Per-route cost controls" guide with screenshots and example policies (doc owner: DevEx).
- Sales enablement: SKU one-pager, pricing calculator, FAQ (owner: GTM).
- Migration playbook: step-by-step checklist for customers switching to billing_v3 (owner: Customer Success).

Appendix A — Example API request (routes cost-control)
-----------------------------------------------------
POST /v1/routes/chat-frontend/cost-control
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "budget_usd_per_day": "500.00",
  "fallback_policy": "permissive",
  "alert_threshold_pct": "80"
}

Appendix B — Rollout checklist (owners must sign off)
----------------------------------------------------
1. QA perf validation complete for 10k qps harness (owner: eng-serving-runtime).
2. Billing event tests with staging invoices (owner: finance-product).
3. Console UX sign-off and docs live (owner: eng-developer-experience).
4. Pilot customer onboarding and feedback captured (owner: customer-success).
